name: release-agent-flow
body: The optional, per-repo release path: a repo may have the `agent-builder` scaffold a generated `release-agent` — a hidden subagent that is the ONLY generated agent granted `git push`/`git tag` (as `ask`, so every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval) plus write access to the repo's release artefacts ON THE MAIN CHECKOUT (releases are made from main; no worktree mirror). That main-write set is determined PER REPO: the agent-builder analyses what the repo's release touches and recommends the set, confirmed via the coordinator interview — it is never a fixed list. The `codebase-navigator` tasks the release-agent ONLY after capturing explicit user consent. Approval surfaces both at dispatch (the navigator's consent) and per command (the `ask` grant). Every other generated agent gets no push/tag grant at all. The release-agent is the deliberate carve-out from the recurring "push/tag remain human-approved acts" law and one of the two agent carve-outs of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`. The binary never pushes or tags (git2 only) and `scripts/release.sh` never pushes — the agent may run the script and then push/tag itself.
